g1.label: 1. People ___ write letters
g1.why: 'Used to' describes a past habit; people wrote letters regularly before email.

g2.label: 2. Children ___ have smartphones
g2.why: Smartphones didn't exist, so it's negative; after 'didn't' we write 'use to', not 'used to'.

g3.label: 3. Grandad ___ repair his radio
g3.why: A repeated past action is described with 'used to' + infinitive.

g4.label: 4. Families ___ have the internet
g4.why: Before the 1990s they had no internet at home, so use the negative 'didn't use to'.

g5.label: 5. People ___ meet friends in person
g5.why: This was a past habit that is less common now, so use 'used to'.

g6.label: 6. Students ___ type their homework
g6.why: They wrote by hand, so it's negative: 'didn't use to' (no -d after didn't).

g7.label: 7. My mum ___ listen to the radio
g7.why: 'Every morning' shows a past routine, so use 'used to'.

g8.label: 8. Shops ___ accept online payments
g8.why: Everyone paid with cash, so the sentence is negative: 'didn't use to'.

g1.label: 1. My grandmother ___ to school
g1.why: 'Every day when she was young' is a past habit, so use 'used to walk'.

g2.label: 2. Yesterday, she ___ to the shop
g2.why: 'Yesterday' is one finished action, so use the simple past, not 'used to'.

g3.label: 3. Last week, our class ___ a museum
g3.why: 'Last week' is a single past event, so use the simple past.

g4.label: 4. In the 1980s, people ___ songs
g4.why: This was a common habit over a period of time, so use 'used to'.

g5.label: 5. Grandad ___ every month for years
g5.why: 'Every single month for years' is a repeated past habit: 'used to write'.

g6.label: 6. He ___ his last letter in 1995
g6.why: One action at a specific time (1995) takes the simple past.

g7.label: 7. Before computers, workers ___ typewriters
g7.why: A general past situation that is no longer true takes 'used to' + infinitive.

g8.label: 8. On that day, the reporter ___
g8.why: 'On that day' is one specific occasion, so use the simple past, not 'used to'.
